steps.title: Import zustand and persist middleware
steps.instruction: Import the 'create' function from 'zustand' and the 'persist' function from 'zustand/middleware'.
steps.hint: Use two separate import statements to bring in the required functions from their respective packages.
steps.seedCode: // Import create from 'zustand' and persist from 'zustand/middleware' here
steps.expectedOutcome: The necessary zustand functions are imported and available for use in the next steps.
successCriteria: The code must include two import statements: one importing 'create' from 'zustand', and another importing 'persist' from 'zustand/middleware'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported the core zustand package and the persist middleware.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing both 'create' from 'zustand' and 'persist' from 'zustand/middleware'.
steps.feedbackWrong: This step requires importing 'create' from 'zustand' and 'persist' from 'zustand/middleware'. Check your import statements.

steps.title: Define the store interface
steps.instruction: Define a TypeScript interface named 'StoreState' with two properties: 'count' of type number and 'name' of type string.
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and property definitions inside curly braces.
steps.seedCode:
// Import create from 'zustand' and persist from 'zustand/middleware' here

// Define the StoreState interface here
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a TypeScript interface that defines the shape of your store's state.
successCriteria: The interface must be named 'StoreState' and include both 'count: number' and 'name: string' properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've correctly defined the StoreState interface with the required typed properties.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your interface is named 'StoreState' and includes both 'count: number' and 'name: string' properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't match what we need. Remember to create a TypeScript interface named 'StoreState' with 'count: number' and 'name: string' properties.

steps.title: Create the store with initial state
steps.instruction: Create a store using create<StoreState>() with initial count: 0 and name: ''
steps.hint: Call create<StoreState>() with a function that returns an object containing count and name properties with their initial values.
steps.expectedOutcome: A Zustand store is created with the initial state values count: 0 and name: ''.
successCriteria: The store is created using create<StoreState>() and returns an object with count and name properties initialized to 0 and ''.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the Zustand store with the correct initial state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that you're using create<StoreState>() and that the initial state includes both count: 0 and name: ''.
steps.feedbackWrong: The store wasn't created correctly. Make sure to use create<StoreState>() and provide an object with count: 0 and name: '' as the initial state.

steps.title: Add increment and decrement actions
steps.instruction: Inside the store creation, add two actions: an increment function that increases count by 1 and a decrement function that decreases count by 1.
steps.hint: In the set function, you can update the count state by accessing the current state and returning the new value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The store now has increment and decrement functions that modify the count state.
successCriteria: The store includes an increment function
The store includes a decrement function
Both functions update the count state correctly
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the increment and decrement actions to your Zustand store. These functions will allow components to modify the count state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure both increment and decrement functions are defined and properly update the count state using the set function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The store doesn't have the required actions. Remember to add both increment and decrement functions inside the store creation that update the count state.

steps.title: Add name update action
steps.instruction: Inside the create function, add a setName action that updates the name property in the store state.
steps.hint: Add a function called setName that takes a new name string and uses the set function to update the name property.
steps.expectedOutcome: The store will have a setName function that can update the name property when called.
successCriteria: The setName function should be defined inside the create callback, take a string parameter, and use set to update the name property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the setName action to update the name in the store.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure setName is defined as a function that takes a string and calls set({ name: newName }).
steps.feedbackWrong: The setName action wasn't added correctly. It should be a function that updates the name property using set.

steps.title: Wrap store with persist middleware
steps.instruction: Wrap the store creation with the persist middleware, passing the store configuration as the first argument and a configuration object with name: 'app-storage' as the second argument.
steps.hint: The persist middleware wraps your store configuration. Use persist((set) => ({...}), { name: 'app-storage' }) as the argument to create().
steps.expectedOutcome: The store will be configured to persist its state to localStorage with the key 'app-storage'.
successCriteria: The store creation is wrapped with persist(), and the configuration object includes name: 'app-storage'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully wrapped the store with the persist middleware. This enables automatic persistence to localStorage.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added the persist middleware, but check the configuration. Make sure you're passing two arguments to persist: the store configuration function and an object with name: 'app-storage'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The persist middleware isn't properly applied. You need to wrap the store configuration with persist() and provide the configuration object.

steps.title: Configure persist storage
steps.instruction: Inside the persist middleware configuration, add a 'storage' property set to 'localStorage'.
steps.hint: The persist middleware accepts a configuration object where you can specify the storage backend.
steps.expectedOutcome: The persist middleware will now use the browser's localStorage to save and load the store state automatically.
successCriteria: The persist configuration includes a 'storage' property with the value 'localStorage'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've configured localStorage as the persistence storage backend. The store state will now be saved to and restored from the browser's localStorage.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the storage configuration isn't quite complete. Make sure you've added the 'storage' property with the correct value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The persist middleware configuration doesn't include localStorage storage. Remember to add the 'storage' property to the persist configuration object.

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement with curly braces to import both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of importing React and useState
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The 'react' package is imported, making React and useState available for use in the component you'll create in the next step.
successCriteria: The code should have an import statement that imports React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and useState. This gives you access to React's core functionality and the useState hook for managing component state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the import statement needs adjustment. Make sure you're importing both React and useState from 'react' using the correct syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statement is missing or incorrect. You need to import both React and useState from the 'react' package.

steps.title: Create the main component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named App that returns JSX. Use TypeScript syntax and specify the return type as JSX.Element.
steps.hint: Define a function called App that returns a JSX element (like a div).
steps.expectedOutcome: A functional component named App is defined with a JSX return statement.
successCriteria: The code defines a function component called App that returns JSX (e.g., a div). The component uses TypeScript syntax with a JSX.Element return type annotation.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the App component. This is the main entry point for your application's UI.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've defined a function named App that returns JSX (like a div). Also ensure you're using TypeScript syntax with a JSX.Element return type.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component isn't properly defined. Create a function called App that returns JSX (e.g., a div). Use TypeScript syntax with a JSX.Element return type annotation.

steps.title: Add count display and buttons
steps.instruction: Inside your component's return statement, add a paragraph to display the current count value and two buttons that call the increment and decrement actions from your store.
steps.hint: Access the count state and increment/decrement actions from your store using the useStore hook. Create a paragraph element with the count value and two button elements with onClick handlers.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will display the current count value and provide buttons to increment and decrement it.
successCriteria: A paragraph element displays the count value
Buttons have onClick handlers that call store actions
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the count display and control buttons. The UI now shows the current count and provides interactive controls.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have: 1) A paragraph showing the count value, 2) Two buttons with onClick handlers, 3) Both buttons calling the appropriate store actions.
steps.feedbackWrong: The count display and buttons aren't properly implemented. Check that you're accessing the store values and actions correctly and that your JSX includes the required elements.

steps.title: Add name input field
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, add an input field that displays the current name from the store and updates it when the user types.
steps.hint: You'll need to access the name state and setName action from your store, then bind them to the input's value and onChange properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will include a text input that shows the persisted name and updates it when typed into.
successCriteria: Add an input element with value bound to the name state and onChange that calls setName with the event target value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a controlled input that displays and updates the persisted name state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the input's value is bound to the name state and onChange properly calls setName with the new value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The input field is missing or not properly connected to the store. Ensure you access the name and setName from useStore and bind them to the input.

steps.title: Add reset functionality
steps.instruction: Add a reset button to your component that, when clicked, calls the store's clearStorage method to clear the persisted data.
steps.hint: Add a button element with an onClick handler that calls useStore.persist.clearStorage().
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of a reset button for a persisted store
<button onClick={() => useStore.persist.clearStorage()}>
  Reset Store
</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a reset button that clears the persisted store data when clicked.
successCriteria: The code should include a button element with an onClick handler that calls useStore.persist.clearStorage().
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a reset button that clears the persisted data when clicked.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a button, but make sure it calls useStore.persist.clearStorage() in the onClick handler.
steps.feedbackWrong: The reset button is missing or doesn't properly call the clearStorage method. Try adding a button with onClick={() => useStore.persist.clearStorage()}.
